वेण् वेण्, cl. 1. P. A. वेणति, -ते, &c.,
to go, move, move about; to play on an
instrument, &c. (= rt. वेन्, q. v.).

वेण, अस्, m. (perhaps connected with वीणा and
meaning ‘a lyre-player’), a musician (one by caste,
the son of a Vaideha by an Amba-ṣṭhī or Amba-
ṣṭha woman; see Manu

); N. of a Rā-
jarshi or royal Ṛṣi (father of Pṛthu, and said to
have perished through irreligious conduct and want
of submissiveness to the Brāhmans; he is represented
as having occasioned confusion of castes, see Manu
VII. 41

, and as founder of the race of
Niṣādas and Dhīvaras; according to the Viṣṇu-
Purāṇa, Veṇa was a son of Aṅga and a descendant of
the first Manu; a Veṇa Rāja-śravas is enumerated
among the Veda-vyāsas or arrangers of the Veda;
cf. वेन); (आ), f., N. of a river.
वेणि वेणि, इस्, f. (according to Uṇādi-s.

IV.
48

. fr. rt. 1. वी, but rather fr. rt. वे), weaving, braid-
ing, braided hair, a braid of hair, hair twisted into
a single unornamented braid and allowed to fall on
the back (as worn by widows and women whose
husbands are absent, as a token of mourning; cf.
एक-वेणि); the conflux or meeting of two or more
rivers or streams in a common point of union (as at
Prayāga or Allahabad, where the Gaṅgā, Yamunā,
and Sarasvatī are supposed to unite; cf. त्रि-वेणी,
प्र-याग).
—वेणि-माधव, अस्, m. a particular
square-shaped idol or stone image of a god at Pra-
yāga.
—वेणि-वेधनी, f. ‘hair-penetrating,’ a leech.
—वेणि-वेधिनी, f. ‘braid-piercer,’ a comb.

वेणी, f. braided hair, &c. = वेणि above; a stream,
current; N. of a river; a sort of grass, Andropogon
Serratum; a ewe.
—वेणी-दास, अस्, m. a proper N.
—वेणी-बन्ध, अस्, m. the binding of the braid
of mourning.
—वेणी-माधव, see वेणि-माधव.
—वेणी-माधव-बन्धु, उस्, m., N. of the father
of Raṅga-nātha.
—वेणी-संहार, अस्, m. ‘braid-
seizing, hair-seizing,’ N. of a well-known drama by
Bhaṭṭa-nārāyaṇa (the subject of which is an incident
described in the Sabhā-parvan of the Mahā-bhārata,
2229-2235, where it is narrated that after Yudhi-
ṣṭhira had lost all his property, including Draupadī,
to Duryodhana in gambling with dice, she was treated
with great indignity by Duḥśāsana, who dragged her
by her braided hair into the public assembly; Bhīma,
who witnessed this insult, swore that in revenge he
would one day dash Duḥśāsana to pieces and drink
his blood — a threat which he fulfilled; this drama is
said to be also called वेणी-संवरण, perhaps for
˚-संहरण).
वेणिका, f. braided hair.

वेणीर वेणीर, अस्, m. the soap-berry, Sa-
pindus Detergens (= अरिष्ट).
वेणु वेणु, उस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s.
III. 38

. fr. वी substituted for rt. अज्, but probably
connected with rt. वे), a bamboo; a reed; a flute,
fife, pipe; N. of a king of the Yādavas.
—वेणु-
कर्कर, अस्, m. a species of thorny plant (= करीर,
commonly called Karir or Karil).
—वेणु-ज, अस्, m.
bamboo seed or fruit.
—वेणु-दत्त, अस्, m. a proper
N.
—वेणु-दल, अम्, n. a small shoot of a cane.
[]
—वेणु-दारि, इस्, m. a proper N.
—वेणु-दारिन्, ई,
m., N. of a demon.
—वेणु-ध्म, अस्, m. a flute-
player, fifer, piper.
—वेणु-निस्रुति, इस्, m. the sugar-
cane.
—वेणु-पत्त्री, f. a species of plant (= वंश-
पत्त्री, हिङ्गु-पर्णी).
—वेणु-यव, अस्, m. bamboo
seed or fruit.
—वेणु-यष्टि, इस्, m. f. a bamboo staff.
—वेणु-वाद or वेणु-वादक, अस्, m. a flute-
player, piper.
—वेणु-वीज, अम्, n. bamboo seed.
—वेणु-हय, अस्, m., N. of a king.
—वेणु-होत्र,
अस्, m., N. of the father of king Bharga; of the
father of Gārgya (according to another account).

वेणुक, अस्, m. a goad with a bamboo handle
(used for driving an elephant).

वेणुन वेणुन, अम्, n. (also read वेणु-ज),
black pepper (= मरिच).

वेणविन्, ई, इनी, इ (fr. वेणु), having a flute or
pipe (said of Śiva).

वेणी-संहार; add — ‘hair-binding,’ (the name
of the Drama, though connected by some with the
seizing and unloosing of Draupadī's hair by Duḥśā-
sana, rather refers to its being bound together again
after the punishment of Duḥśāsana.)
